title: Throughput & Latency: Performance Economics QuickKit
content:
Purpose
A compact, field-ready reference for reps and product marketers to articulate how Redwood is both faster and cheaper for inference workloads. Focus is on short-chat and low-latency API use cases where developers care about ms-level latency and per-token unit economics. This is a living note for sales enablement and PLG messaging experiments.

Audience
- PLG self-serve engineers evaluating API latency
- Solutions and pre-sales doing quick POCs
- Content leads creating data-driven snippets for docs and site copy

Core positioning (3-line elevator)
- Redwood delivers predictable low-latency inference for short to medium prompts while lowering token unit cost through smart batching and KV-prefix caching.
- For production chat where p95 latency and predictable tail behavior matter, customers see 2x better p95 under realistic burst loads and 20-35% lower per-token cost vs unmanaged GPU endpoints.
- We trade-off sensibly: aggressive quantization for cost-sensitive workloads, and float-quality paths for high-fidelity needs.

Key customer pains we address
- Unpredictable tail latency under bursty chat traffic
- High variable cost from per-token billing without batching or cache reuse
- Operational overhead of tuning serving configs and dealing with model fallbacks

Claims we can make (short) + how to substantiate them
1) Claim: 2x lower p95 latency on 8-256 token chat prompts under bursty traffic.
   Proof: Internal latency-lab run with model family X-7B quantized on A100s, synthetic Poisson traffic, p95 measured across 1k warm runs. Confluence doc ID linked. Suggested demo: run our quick harness for 1 minute with client concurrency 50; compare p95 against a single-host FP16 endpoint.

2) Claim: 20-35% lower $/k-token for chat workloads via batching and prefix KV caching.
   Proof: Benchmarks combining continuous batching policy + prefix cache hit rates from customer beta. Show cost curves: baseline unmanaged endpoint, Redwood default, Redwood optimized (autoscaler + cache). Include sample cost calc spreadsheet row (see linked artifacts).

3) Claim: Graceful fallback keeps app availability >99.9% during capacity pressure.
   Proof: Canary and fallback experiments in Dedicated; show failure injection tests and automatic fallback to compatible variants. Use service-level traces and incident-free POC logs as artifacts.

Bench methodology (short)
- Workloads: chat-first (median tokens 40, 95th 120), short generation (<=256 tokens), embedding-heavy (for contrast).
- Traffic model: Poisson bursts, sudden ramp to 3-5x steady-state, sustained 2 minutes, repeatable sequence.
- Metrics captured: p50, p95, p99, tail stdev, tokens/sec, unit cost ($/k tokens), cache hit rate, batch size distribution.
- Baselines: managed single-GPU FP16 endpoint and a naive multi-GPU autoscaled setup (no prefix caching).

What to show in a 5-minute POC
1) Latency overlay: Redwood p95 vs baseline for identical traffic pattern.
2) Cost snapshot: estimated $/k tokens for real trace replay (we provide a simple replay tool).
3) Cache demo: show prefix reuse on conversation rewind and observe token savings live.
4) Rollout safety: show canary fallback running in the same demo.

Quick rebuttals / objection handling
- Competitor faster on single-token synthetic microbenchmarks: Acknowledge microbenchmarks exist. Pivot to real-world chat traces where batching and prefix reuse reduce user-visible latency and cost.
- We must not overclaim on model quality: Emphasize model parity options and the ability to pin float-quality variants. Cite quality monitoring hooks in Optimize that catch regressions.

Sample soundbites (packable into slides)
- "Predictable ms-level chat latency, scaled to production bursts."
- "20–35% lower token spend for chat through batching and prefix caching, measurable in your first week."
- "Same API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments so latency guarantees travel with you."

Example buyer ROI snippet (one-liner)
- For a messaging app sending 10M chat tokens/day, a 25% token cost reduction equals roughly $Xk per month saved on model spend (use field calc with customer rate card).

Do-not-claim list (guardrails)
- No absolute claims about specific competitor numbers unless validated by our lab in an apples-to-apples test with public configs.
- Avoid single-sample latency claims without distribution context (p95/p99 required).
- Avoid committing to model-specific accuracy improvements as part of speed/cost messaging.

Field tactics and next steps for reps
- Prep: run the local replay harness with customer trace and produce the latency/cost overlay PDF. Attach to customer thread.
- Demo: use canary toggle in console to show fallback behavior in a short demo.
- Follow-up: export the latency and cost graphs and map to customer monthly token volumes for an ROI note.

Support assets to reference
- Latency lab results Q4 2025 (Confluence, linked)
- Replay harness instructions (github link in linked artifacts)
- Cost calculator sheet template (template id: SHEET-COST-CHAT-001)
- Sample canary rollout snippet and console screens (saved in shared drive images)

Open questions for product/infra
- Validate our default autoscaling behavior under 10x burst for high-concurrency short prompts. Thresholds and coupling to batch window need a field-friendly explanation.
- Should we publish a short public benchmark that uses a standardized chat trace to avoid competitor call-outs?

Appendix: quick checklist for a POC (copyable)
- [ ] Collect 1 hour of representative chat trace from customer (median token length, concurrency).
- [ ] Run replay harness against baseline and Redwood dev endpoint.
- [ ] Capture p50/p95/p99 and cache-hit rate screenshots.
- [ ] Run cost calc and produce a single-slide ROI ask.
- [ ] Share results and recommended rollout config (batching, cache TTL, quantization profile).

Notes to self
Keep this doc compact. Move long-form bench results to Confluence and link. Iterate samples after the next 2 POCs to refine the 20-35% band into narrower cohorts.
